recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. Do not duplicate the rule on source/http.html unless a future work group decision asks for a navigation-only editorial restructure, because the authoritative Search Inputs section already conveys the behavior and duplicating it would risk maintenance drift.
issue_request: FHIR-19523 was Published with a Persuasive resolution. It requested explicit FHIR-core HTTP/search wording that a resource search with no search parameters, such as GET [base]/Practitioner, returns all instances of that resource, while allowing servers to prohibit queries without or with insufficient parameters.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been initially applied by 142ad7624ca77d81a9463a6ddbd278f521a109da, which added a source/search.html paragraph saying that searches with no filters, such as GET [base]/Patient or POST [base]/Patient/_search with an empty body, should return all records and noting that servers may prohibit insufficiently constrained queries.
additional_context: FHIR-20392 is the same no-filter search behavior family and is already separately represented on the combined branch. Its implementation commit 6600a9d1738b011230210afa99d7dbc7ea1cef89 refined the wording to cover both system and type search contexts and to require an appropriate error when a server rejects an overly broad search. Later edits only added conformance markup and punctuation cleanup. The Jira-linked Zulip thread for FHIR-19523 confirms that the behavior was considered implicit and the tracker was intended as a clarification.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/search.html lines 232-235 already state that, in the absence of any search filters, GET [base], GET [base]/Patient, POST [base]/_search, and POST [base]/Patient/_search with no body SHOULD return all records in scope of the search context, and that servers MAY reject overly broad searches with an appropriate error.
